stories.headline: Indian opposition MPs detained in protest against election chief
stories.title: Indian opposition MPs detained in protest against election chief
stories.summary: Opposition leaders have alleged that CEC Gyanesh Kumar manipulated voter rolls to favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi's party during elections.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Police in Delhi detained several opposition lawmakers as they tried to march demanding the chief election commissioner resign over a controversial voter roll revision.
Main opposition leader Rahul Gandhi, his sister Priyanka and other MPs were forced into a police bus.
Released shortly after, they resumed their march and began a sit-in near Election Commission headquarters.
It is the latest escalation in a growing row over a nationwide revision of voter rolls.

Opposition parties accuse Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of overseeing a process that could benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), an allegation both the BJP and Election Commission have rejected.
"Some of the MPs tried to take some other roads to the Election Commission building.

We have officers stationed at multiple points, from where the protesters were picked up in buses and taken to different police stations," Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police Manjeet Sheoran told the BBC.
The police did not disclose how many lawmakers had been detained.
The opposition said 237 MPs from a range of parties participated in the march.

Tuesday's protest came just four days after the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a Gen Z-backed online satirical movement, organised demonstrations in Mumbai and Delhi, also demanding the CEC's resignation.
The group has described those demonstrations as the beginning of a nationwide campaign and has called for another round of protests on 10 October.
At the centre of the controversy is the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

stories.headline: UN is ‘irrelevant’ but must be fixed, not bypassed, says Jaishankar
stories.title: UN is ‘irrelevant’ but must be fixed, not bypassed, says Jaishankar
stories.summary: The United Nations (UN) has become gridlocked and ineffective on the biggest issues of the day, said Foreign Minister S Jaishankar on Monday, arguing that the world needs the body and should reform it rather than work around it.“It’s obvious to everybody by now that the UN is gridlocked,” Jaishankar said at the concluding session of the fifth Kautilya Economic Conclave in New Delhi.He cited conflicts in the Gulf and Ukraine, issues in Africa and even the Covid-19 pandemic, where, he said, the UN had been “largely irrelevant to the decision-making”. Jaishankar later said “ineffectiveness” was the better word.Also Read: Strait of Hormuz shows economic risk of geography: PK MishraBlaming the UN Security Council’s (UNSC’s) structure, he said it no longer represents the entirety of the global interest.“The UN started with 51 members. It’s got almost four times that number today. So, if you have grown four times and you want to keep the old board of management, it’s not going to work. It’s common sense.”Jaishankar, who recently addressed the 81st session of the UN General Assembly, said the world needs the UN. “The UN has done a big service to the international community. Our job must be to fix the UN, not to work around the UN.”The other panellist at the session, former Singapore foreign minister George Yong Boon Yeo, argued that the US had undermined the institutions it once built, and that Asia should build regional structures. He said India and China held near-identical positions on Ukraine and global institutions, and that, if they stood together, “many structures will hold”.“The WTO can continue without the US. The WHO is continuing without the US… India, Asean and China can work together,” said Yeo.Jaishankar rejected the premise, saying “we can’t seriously look at a global trading system without the United States”.“The US is such a major trading power and is the biggest economy. So the idea that a few countries come together and then try to fix the problem because the US is a problem… I don’t think that’s a viable option,” he said.He said the US wasn’t to blame for all the trade problems. “A lot of the market distortions which have come into the trading system have not come from the US.”On the Ukraine conflict, Jaishankar said India had long held that the war is unlikely to be resolved on the battlefield. “And, therefore, it was important to have negotiations between the parties. Dialogue and diplomacy were probably the best pathway.”He criticised peace gatherings held without Moscow. “We always felt, what is the point of having a gathering dealing with the Ukraine conflict where Russia is not there?”He said India’s involvement deepened after an attack on a ship which killed Indian sailors. Those talks widened to cover grain shipments from the Black Sea and then energy. “We still keep in touch with both sides,” Jaishankar said.Asked how India looks at its ties with the US, China, Russia and Europe, Jaishankar said that we are moving towards a multipolar world, whose architecture and geometry are very different from the way they used to be before.Also Read: War in Iran: How India's biggest companies are feeling the heat“Given India’s perspective, I would argue that actually every relationship, net-net, is a plus.”On India’s role for developing nations, he said: “The Global South does expect a country like India to go up on that stage and articulate [its concerns]. Somebody has to do it. And that somebody, in the eyes of many countries, is a country like India.”“We may be, in many ways, unique, but we are not distant from the world. We are very connected, and we feel that obligation to build that into our foreign policy.”

stories.headline: Supreme Court gets three new judges as CJI Surya Kant administers oath
stories.title: Supreme Court gets three new judges as CJI Surya Kant administers oath
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 6 : Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Tuesday administered the oath of office to three new judges of the Supreme Court -- Justices Sunita Agarwal, Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya, and Aparesh Kumar Singh. The swearing-in ceremony, which was live-streamed, was held at 3.30 p.m., marking a departure from the usual practice of administering the oath to newly appointed Supreme Court judges in the morning. Newly appointed Supreme Court judges usually take the oath of office at 10.30 a.m., coinciding with the time when the top court assembles on working days to conduct hearings. The three Chief Justices of the High Courts took the oath as judges of the apex court after the Centre cleared their elevation on the recommendation of the Supreme Court Collegium this week. "The Supreme Court Collegium in its meeting held on 28th September, 2026 has recommended elevation of the following Chief Justices of the High Courts as Judges in the Supreme Court," the Collegium had said in a statement uploaded on the apex court's official website. Acting swiftly on the Collegium's recommendation, the Centre on Monday approved the elevation of Justices Agarwal, Upadhyaya, and Singh. In a post on X, Union Minister for Law and Justice Arjun Ram Meghwal announced that the President, after consultation with CJI Surya Kant, had appointed the three Chief Justices as judges of the apex court. Justice Agarwal, born on April 30, 1966, was appointed as a judge of the Allahabad High Court on November 21, 2011. She became the Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court on July 23, 2023. Justice Upadhyaya, born on June 16, 1965, was appointed as a puisne Judge of the Allahabad High Court on November 21, 2011 and became a permanent Judge on August 6, 2013. He became the Senior Judge of the Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court on March 28, 2023. He was appointed Chief Justice of the Bombay High Court and took the oath on July 29, 2023, before being transferred as Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court, where he took the oath on January 21, 2025. Justice Singh, born on July 7, 1965, was appointed as an Additional Judge of the Jharkhand High Court on January 24, 2012 and was confirmed as a Permanent Judge on January 16, 2014. He served as Acting Chief Justice of the Jharkhand High Court from December 20, 2022, to February 19, 2023. He took the oath as Chief Justice of the Tripura High Court on April 17, 2023, and was subsequently transferred as Chief Justice of the Telangana High Court, where he took the oath on July 19, 2025. The appointments will further strengthen the Supreme Court's judicial strength following the Centre's decision earlier this year to increase the sanctioned strength to 37, excluding the CJI. --IANS

stories.title: Supreme Court stay lifts Tata Chemicals off day’s low
stories.summary: Tata Chemicals informed BSE and NSE that the Supreme Court has restrained the Government of Gujarat and others from taking any coercive action against the company in an ongoing land-rights case

article_sentences: Shares of Tata Chemicals Limited are trading near flat on Tuesday after touching an intraday high of ₹624.75, aided by a Supreme Court order that emerged last trading session.
The stock was at ₹617.20 at 15.05, down a marginal 0.03 per cent from its previous close of ₹617.40, having opened higher at ₹620.
Total traded value stood at ₹37.41 crore on a volume of 6.04 lakh shares, with the stock part of the Nifty Smallcap 100 index.
Sell-side pressure remains dominant, with 70.52 per cent of pending orders on the sell side against 29.48 per cent on the buy side.
Deliverable quantity stands at 49.29 per cent of traded volume, suggesting a mix of positional and intraday interest.
Annualised volatility is elevated at 45.47 per cent.

Tata Chemicals informed BSE and NSE that the Supreme Court, vide its order dated October 5, 2026, has restrained the Government of Gujarat and others from taking any coercive action against the company in an ongoing land-rights case.
The court has also issued a notice to the state government seeking its response.

The dispute pertains to Writ Petition No. 26530, filed by the company before the Gujarat High Court, concerning its pre-existing rights over land at Mithapur, Gujarat, on which legacy open wastewater channels ran into the sea.
Tata Chemicals had first informed the exchanges about the High Court proceedings on May 26, 2026.

The stock remains under significant pressure on a longer horizon — down 33.44 per cent over one year and 17.89 per cent year-to-date, against the Nifty 500’s -4.45 per cent and -7.41 per cent respectively.
Its 52-week high was ₹944.50 hit in October 2025.

stories.title: Cabinet Clears ₹10,000 Cr SME Fund To Back Manufacturing, Tech Focused SMEs
stories.summary: The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has approved the government’s ₹10,000 Cr SME Growth Fund (SGF) to…

article_sentences: The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has approved the government’s ₹10,000 Cr SME Growth Fund (SGF) to offer growth credit capital to small and medium enterprises.
Announced in Budget 2026-27, the fund will invest in high-potential SMEs across manufacturing, services, technology, innovation-driven sectors and strategic value chains.
A majority of the allocation of the fund will go towards manufacturing-focused enterprises.
The initiative aims to widen access to equity and liquidity for MSMEs and help promising Indian businesses scale into globally competitive companies.
The SGF is meant to fill the gap in growth capital for SMEs, as most existing funds focus on early-stage and micro enterprises.
Under the framework, the government will commit ₹10,000 Cr to alternative investment funds (AIFs), that will subsequently invest in high-potential SMEs.
This will help businesses expand operations, increase manufacturing capacity, adopt new technologies, enter international markets and integrate into global supply chains.
Centre's MSME Funding Push.
The SGF is part of the government’s wider push to support the MSME sector via credit, digitalisation, ease of doing business, public procurement and other initiatives.
The fund will also support SMEs in industrial clusters across Tier II and Tier III cities, with the aim of strengthening local supply chains and creating jobs.

As part of the ‘Creating Champion MSMEs’ strategy announced in Budget 2026-27, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman had also proposed an additional ₹2,000 Cr for ‘Self-Reliant India Fund’ to support micro enterprises and provide them with access to risk capital.
The Budget also proposed several measures to improve cash flow for MSMEs through the Trade Receivables e-Discounting System (TReDS).

stories.headline: Cabinet approves proposal to set up Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority
stories.title: Cabinet approves proposal to set up Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority
stories.summary: The ITLA will prepare a long-term Transport Plan covering roads, railways, ports, civil aviation and urban mobility, and evaluate government infrastructure projects worth ₹500 crore or more
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Cabinet on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) approved a proposal to set up an Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority (ITLA), Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said.
The authority will function as the apex body for integrated transport and logistics planning, research, project appraisal and monitoring, policy support and data analytics.
The ITLA will prepare a long-term Transport Plan covering roads, railways, ports and shipping, civil aviation, inland waterways, coastal shipping, urban mobility and logistics, Mr. Vaishnaw said.
The decision to set up the ITLA was taken at a meeting of the Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

The Cabinet "approved the setting up of a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV), namely, Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority (ITLA), to strengthen research, planning, appraisal, monitoring and impact assessment within the broad domains of transportation and logistics," an official statement said.
The approval seeks to address long-standing challenges arising from fragmented planning and implementation across multiple transport-related Ministries and agencies.
By fostering greater coordination and multi-modal integration, the ITLA is expected to enhance the efficiency, sustainability and effectiveness of transport infrastructure development in India.

The authority will evaluate short-term sectoral plans (of about five years) and annual plans of transport Ministries to ensure consistency and alignment with the National Transport Master Plan, and promote multi-modal infrastructure development.
It will also undertake technical appraisal of government infrastructure projects costing ₹500 crore or more.
Financial appraisal will continue to be carried out through existing mechanisms.
The authority will monitor the implementation of transport and infrastructure projects worth more than ₹500 crore, and provide a coordinated mechanism for issue resolution.
It will undertake a post-implementation impact assessment of these projects.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Gets 3 Women Judges With Justice Sunita Agarwal's Elevation
stories.title: Supreme Court Gets 3 Women Judges With Justice Sunita Agarwal's Elevation
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: With the appointment of Justice Sunita Agarwal, former Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court, the Supreme Court now has three sitting women judges.

The highest number of women judges the Supreme Court had at a time was 4, when Justices Indira Banerjee, Hima Kohli, BV Nagarathna and Bela Trivedi were present simultaneously from August 2021 till Justice Banerjee's retirement in September 2022.
Justice Hima Kohli retired in September 2024 followed by Justice Bela M. Trivedi in May 2025.
After Justice Trivedi retired in May 2025, Justice Nagarathna was the sole woman judge until the elevation of Justice Mohana a year later.
Notably, this is the second appointment of a woman judge by the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant-led Collegium after Justice Mohana.

With the present additions, the Supreme Court's working strength stands at 37 judges, with one vacancy against the sanctioned strength of 38 judges, which will be reduced to one more with the upcoming retirement of Justice Satish Chandra Sharma in November.
It may be noted that the sanctioned strength was increased from 34 to 38 judges recently.

Appearing before Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant, senior advocates Vikas Singh and Shadan Farasat, for the State government, said the order violated the very basic principles of federalism.
Mr. Singh said the State was poll-bound, and a Central agency has been ordered to investigate allegations.

The very federal structure has been violated,” he submitted.

stories.headline: Harmanpreet Kaur steps down as India captain, ends leadership stint
stories.title: Harmanpreet Kaur steps down as India captain, ends leadership stint
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 6 : Indian women’s ODI World Cup winning skipper Harmanpreet Kaur has stepped down from captaincy across all formats after serving as the full-time T20I captain since 2018 and as the ODI captain since 2022, having taken over the reins from the legendary Mithali Raj. “Today, I step down as captain of the Indian Women’s Cricket Team across all formats. This is not an easy decision. It carries years of memories, emotions, sacrifices, and moments that will stay with me for the rest of my life," Kaur wrote on Instagram. "I have given everything I had to this team and to Indian women’s cricket — my blood, my sweat, my time, and many times, a part of my own game and personal ambitions. There were moments when I had to put my individual performance, my own growth, and what I wanted for myself aside, because I believed the team had to come first. “As a captain, I have had to make difficult decisions. Decisions that were not always understood, not always easy, and sometimes came at a personal cost. But every decision I made was with one intention - to make this TEAM better and to give other players the opportunity to grow, believe in themselves and become the best versions of themselves,” she added. She etched her name in history books by becoming the first female skipper to lead the Indian team to a maiden senior ICC World Cup title by defeating South Africa on home soil. “I have seen it all. I have seen the lowest moments, the heartbreak, the criticism, the doubts and the days when nothing seemed to go our way. And I have also experienced the highest highs - the victories, the celebrations, the pride of representing our country, and the moments that made every sacrifice worth it,” Kaur wrote. Harman also led the side to a record four Asia Cup titles as captain in 2012, 2016, 2022, 2026 and also guided the team to consecutive gold medals at the Asian Games, finishing on top of the podium in Hangzhou 2022 and Aichi-Nagoya 2026. “I leave the captaincy today with a heart full of emotions , but also with PEACE. Because I genuinely believe my team is in a good place. A team with talent, character, belief and a future that I am incredibly excited to watch and be a part of. I feel I have done my duty. I gave this team everything I had. I carried the responsibility with pride, and I will always be grateful for the privilege of leading Indian women’s cricket. Now, it is time for me to turn the page. “Captaincy may end today, but my love for Indian cricket never will. Thank you to every teammate, coach, support staff, management , BCCI , family members every single fan who stood by me through the highs and lows. Blood. Sweat. Sarifice. Pride. I gave it all. Now, I’m ready to play for the love of the game again. Captaincy ends. The journey continues,” she concluded. Harman’s other major notable achievements as captain include leading India to their first bilateral Women's ODI series win on English soil since 1999, when the team clinched a historic win in 2022. She also commanded the team to a historic Test match win against Australia in 2023 and a breakthrough T20I series victory against England in 2025. She also surpassed leading men's captains like MS Dhoni and Rohit Sharma to become the first cricketer to captain a side in 150+ T20I matches. Under her leadership, the team defeated England by 270 runs in the first-ever women's Test match played at Lord's Cricket Ground earlier this year. --IANS

stories.title: Supreme Court 7-Judge Bench Disposes Reference On Legislative Privilege As Infructuous
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today closed the 7-judge reference on the issue of legislative privileges vis-a-vis free speech, noting that the 2003 resolution of the Tamil Nadu legislative assembly, which was the trigger for the case, was withdrawn in 2004.

A bench comprising CJI Surya Kant, Justice Aravind Kumar, Justice PK Mishra, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice Vipul Pancholi, Justice Shree Chandrashekhar and Justice V Mohana was constituted to hear the matter, which had been pending for nearly 2 decades.
Today, while disposing of the matter as infructuous, the bench noted that the withdrawal of the impugned resolution skipped the notice of the Court while passing the reference order.
The bench observed that the cause of action for the reference has become infructuous, and closed the matter.
However, the bench left the questions of law open for adjudication in an appropriate case.
After the order was dictated, Senior Advocate AM Singhvi commented in a lighter vein that the Court has set two records - shortest hearing and quickest disposal of a 7-judge matter.
Yesterday, on mentioning of the matter, CJI Surya Kant had expressed that the reference might be disposed of as an academic issue.
The reference originated from the 2003 case N. Ravi.
Speaker, Legislative Assembly, Chennai, challenging the 2003 decision taken by the Tamil Nadu assembly to sentence 5 journalists of The Hindu for articles criticizing the State Government.
The matter was ultimately referred to the 7-judge bench to examine the interplay between Articles 194(3), 19(1)(a) and 21 of the Constitution.
The reference remained pending for over two decades, and the Court, in August 2026, decided to commence the hearing from October 6.
Yesterday, Senior Advocate Raju Ramachandran, for the State of Tamil Nadu, informed a 3-judge bench led by CJI Surya Kant that the 2003 resolution of the Assembly was revoked in 2004 itself.

stories.headline: CM Omar questions sudden action against Rohingyas, says ‘targeted for no reason’
stories.title: CM Omar questions sudden action against Rohingyas, says ‘targeted for no reason’
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 06: Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Tuesday questioned the “sudden” action being taken against Rohingyas, saying they were being “targeted for no reason”, while asserting that people who entered India from Bangladesh without permission could not stay in the country illegally. “People who have come from Bangladesh without permission, it is a different matter for them. But the Rohingyas, who are being targeted for no reason, when they were deported from their country, we gave them a place here. We allowed them to live here until their country’s situation improves,” Omar told reporters in Srinagar. “I find it strange to take action against them suddenly. But we do not have it in our hands. This is the Government of India,” he said. Omar added that the J&K Police is also not under the control of the Union Territory government in the matter. On the Uniform Civil Code (UCC), the Chief Minister said the J&K government would not implement it, arguing that such legislation should be debated and enacted by Parliament. “If you have the courage, bring a law in Parliament. Debate it in Parliament. See if it passes in Parliament or not,” he said. On the INDIA bloc’s campaign over alleged deletions from voter lists, Omar said the issue would continue to be raised, noting that the Supreme Court had also sought responses from the Election Commission and the Government of India over the alleged deletions. On mobile connectivity, Omar said the Cabinet had decided to allot land to BSNL in areas without mobile coverage to facilitate the installation of towers. He also said ducts were being laid along roads to avoid repeated digging by different departments for water, electricity and telecommunications works. “Where the road will be built, it would be better to use the duct so that there will be no need to dig the road again and again,” he said.—(KNO)

article_sentences: Deepika T.C. captained India to victory in the first Women’s T20 World Cup for the Blind in November 2025.
Nearly a year later, she is still waiting for the house site that leaders and officials promised her.
She and her 15 teammates, who won the tournament hosted jointly by India and Sri Lanka, say they are unable to get the support they need from society and the government in their day-to-day lives.
They do not get playgrounds and fitness guidance in their localities, and they cannot afford training in big cities.
Leaders who make tall promises in public have shown little interest in ensuring government jobs and house sites for them, they said.
Ms. Deepika hails from Madakasira in Sri Sathya Sai district.
“Due to our partial vision issues, we cannot move around government offices to follow up on house site issues.
The government has to do its own and instill confidence among us,” she told.
The Hindu.
Ms. Deepika, who developed vision problems as an infant, completed a degree course and focused on cricket in spite of her family’s financial struggles.
Her parents, Timmappa and Chittemma, encouraged her to practise cricket in Bengaluru although they had many fears about her partial vision.
She has been consistently playing well and won special recognition when she scored 92 runs off 45 balls against Australia in a World Cup match.

stories.headline: 'Tried To Softly Bend Law Towards Justice': Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya Bids Farewell To Delhi High Court
stories.title: 'Tried To Softly Bend Law Towards Justice': Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya Bids Farewell To Delhi High Court
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'chief justice' in title weight 42
article_sentences: Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya on Tuesday bid farewell to the Delhi High Court on his elevation to the Supreme Court of India, saying that throughout his judicial career, he had tried to “bind law, justice, and compassion together.”

A function was organized by the Delhi High Court today in order to bid farewell to CJ Upadhyaya, which was attended by all the judges as well as Central and Delhi Government counsels as well as lawyers.
On September 28, the Supreme Court Collegium had recommended elevation of Justice Upadhyaya.
Yesterday evening, the Central Government notified his appointment.
In his farewell address, CJ Upadhyaya reflected on his journey from practising as an advocate in Lucknow to serving on the Bench and eventually heading the Delhi High Court.
“Like other judges, I came across unforeseen situations when law was not able to ensure a just outcome in the case, and it appeared isolated from justice.
In such situations, I tried to softly bend the law towards justice for the deserving litigant, and to be able to do so has been a blessing for me,” he said.
Justice Upadhyaya, however, added that he could not himself determine whether he had succeeded in imparting justice.
“I cannot tell whether or not I have succeeded in imparting justice.
In fact, I should not even try because it would be an act of deciding my own cause,” he remarked.

He said that judgeship had given him “a great sense of satisfaction” by providing him with an opportunity to mitigate the sufferings of litigants and fulfil the constitutional promise of justice to citizens.
Recalling his early days as an advocate in Lucknow, Justice Upadhyaya said he had begun his legal career under the guidance of his father and other senior members of the Lucknow Bar.

In fact, I should not even try because it would be an act of deciding my own cause,” he remarked.

He said that judgeship had given him “a great sense of satisfaction” by providing him with an opportunity to mitigate the sufferings of litigants and fulfil the constitutional promise of justice to citizens.

sentences.text: On September 28, the Supreme Court Collegium had recommended elevation of Justice Upadhyaya.

Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya on Tuesday bid farewell to the Delhi High Court on his elevation to the Supreme Court of India, saying that throughout his judicial career, he had tried to “bind law, justice, and compassion together.”

A function was organized by the Delhi High Court today in order to bid farewell to CJ Upadhyaya, which was attended by all the judges as well as Central and Delhi Government counsels as well as lawyers.
Yesterday evening, the Central Government notified his appointment.

article_sentences: Tech Mahindra, Titan, Bajaj Finance and ITC were the top Sensex losers, falling up to 2.3%.
Capital goods, banking, pharma stocks led the gains with the BSE Capital goods index rising 1333 pts to 75,749, pharma index gaining 552 pts and BSE bankex ending 330 pts higher at 62,118.
Sunny Agrawal, Deputy Vice President - Fundamental Research at SBI Securities said, "Market gained for the 2nd consecutive session as global cues remained supportive.
Stocks reporting their 2QFY27 business updates were in focus with Honasa Consumer, Meesho, Trent, Dabur closing higher by 8%, 6%, 12% and 3% respectively in today's session following strong updates.
US Futures are trading 0.5% higher currently.
The US 10-year yield at 5.27% has also come off slightly from the morning highs, lending strength to the Indian market."

Ajit Mishra, SVP – research, Religare Broking said, "Markets extended their recovery on the weekly expiry day, with the benchmarks gaining nearly a percent as easing crude prices and encouraging Q2 business updates supported the sentiment.
Technically, the 22,800–22,850 zone is likely to act as the immediate hurdle, followed by the broader resistance around 23,000-23,200 while 22,600-22,400 remains the key near-term support.
With the broader market structure remaining cautious amid elevated global macro risks, volatility is likely to stay high, favouring a selective, stock-specific approach as opportunities emerge."
Global market signals turned relatively favourable as Brent crude prices eased below the $100-per-barrel mark, supported by stable oil prices and an increase in crude exports from West Asia.
The decline in energy prices offers some relief on the inflation front and provided a supportive backdrop for equities.
Domestic investors, meanwhile, will be focused on the Reserve Bank of India’s Monetary Policy Committee meeting scheduled for tomorrow.

stories.headline: Cabinet nod to new team for transport, logistics
stories.title: Cabinet nod to new team for transport, logistics
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet nod' in title weight 40
article_sentences: The new authority would strengthen research, planning, appraisal, monitoring and impact assessment across the transportation and logistics sectors.
It would work towards harmonising planning, appraisal and monitoring of transport projects.
The ITLA will bring policy research, project planning & appraisal, monitoring & evaluation, and data analytics together under one roof.
ITLA will serve as the apex body for integrated transport and logistics planning in India.
The authority would be responsible to appraise the government infrastructure projects costing Rs 500 crore or more to ensure integrated multi-modal planning.
It will also monitor such transport and infrastructure projects, coordinate issue resolution and assess post-completion impact.
Its key role also includes the preparation of a long term transport plan covering roads, railways, ports, aviation, inland waterways, coastal shipping, urban mobility and logistics.
It would also integrate GSTN e-way bill, FASTag, Vahan, GPS and urban traffic data; use freight-flow and origin-destination analytics for evidence based project planning.
The authority would advise and assist in reviewing and updating the National Logistics Policy, 2022 and support training, skilling and capacity building across logistics sector.
It will also promote research and innovation in transport and logistics sector.

Establishment of the ITLA will play a pivotal role in realizing India’s Vision 2047 by strengthening multimodal connectivity, improving infrastructure efficiency, reducing logistics costs, and enhancing India’s global logistics competitiveness, the government said in a release.
